message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is special because it can be worth **either 1 point or 11 points**—whichever benefits your hand more. Here’s how it works:

| Situation | How the Ace counts |
|-----------|--------------------|
| You’re dealt an Ace first | It starts as 11 (unless you already have another Ace or a high total) |
| You have a “soft” hand (e.g., Ace‑7 = 18) | The Ace stays 11 unless you take another card that would make you bust; then it automatically switches to 1 |
| You have two Aces (e.g., Ace‑Ace) | One Ace counts as 11, the other as 1 → total 12 |
| You’re dealt an Ace later in the round | If counting it as 11 would bust you, it’s treated as 1 instead |

So the Ace gives you flexibility: you can use it as a “high” value (11) when it helps, but it will never force you over 21—it’ll drop to 1 if needed. This dual nature is why Aces are so valuable in Blackjack.
